issues.description: Visibility mismatch for core PersonService methods: in the template PersonService.savePerson(...) and PersonService.deletePerson(...) are declared public, while in the solution they are declared protected. The PersonResource (solution) calls personService.savePerson(...) and personService.deletePerson(...). Because PersonResource is in a different package (de.tum.in.ase.eist.rest) than PersonService (de.tum.in.ase.eist.service), protected visibility does not allow those calls across packages. This inconsistency will cause compilation/access issues and confuses students implementing the REST endpoints (they expect to forward to public service methods as shown in the template and described by the exercise). The problem statement also warns not to change attributes of PersonService, implying service API stability — changing visibility breaks that expectation.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the service methods accessible consistently across artifacts. Restore public visibility for the PersonService methods used by the REST layer (e.g., declare savePerson(...) and deletePerson(...) as public) so PersonResource in de.tum.in.ase.eist.rest can call them. Alternatively, if protected visibility was intentional, move or refactor the REST layer to the same package or expose public wrapper methods — but the simplest fix preserving the intended API is to declare these service methods public, matching the template and the expectation in the problem statement.
